newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI to use Johnson cash to fund Lonrho buy.
newsitem.headline: JCI to use Johnson cash to fund Lonrho buy.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd on Friday said it would use the 105 million stg proceeds of the sale of its stake in Britain's Johnson Matthey Plc to help funds its buy of a slice of Lonrho Plc.
JCI is exploring ways to fund a buy of 26.8 percent of British conglomerate Lonrho Plc for some 2.5 billion rand.
"The cash proceeds from the sale of the Johnson Matthey stake will be used to fund partially the acquisition of the Lonrho shares," the firm said in a statement.

Analysts had been expecting the Johnson Matthey sale and are speculating on other options such as the sale or merger of its unlisted Tavistock coal division with Lonrho and the disposal of non-core assets such as a 9.8 percent stake in Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd.
JCI said it had sold its 18.9 million share stake in Johnson through investment bank SBC Warburg at 5.55 stg per share.
Johnson Matthey chief executive Gordon Thorburn told Reuters he understood the stock had been placed with a number of institutional investors.
